messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: streaming-service-high-tail-latency detected in eu-west-1. p99 spike > 8s, p95 > 2.5s across SSE and websocket paths. Automations flagged proxy pool > 70% queued writes. Paging oncall @maria (severity: sev3). https://runbooks.redwood.example/streaming-latency

alex: seeing it on dashboards too. p95 jumped at 03:02 UTC, p99 at 03:04. Checking traces now.

maria: on it. any known deploys in last 30m?

sam: not that I see. Last deploy was 02:20 for a canary that rolled back.

jia: quick note: customer reports of "streaming pauses" from fintech partner in eu-west. they DM'ed support at 03:06.

alex: grabbing a few logs from the proxy tier. looks like write buffers oscillating between full and drained. stack:
```
proxy.write_queue.length: 0 -> 1200 -> 10 -> 800 -> ...
socket.write_backpressure: true when queue > 600
upstream_latency_ms: 20-40
client_ack_delay_ms: 150-2400
```

maria: that pattern smells like consumer-side pacing + proxy keepalive churn. Are clients hitting slow-consumer bursts?

sam: telemetry shows a cohort of long-poll clients with TCP window shrink. Could be intermittent mobile networks during EU morning. However load on proxy pool also spiked concurrently. We may be running into too-small write buffers under high concurrency.

alex: running quick calc: concurrent streams ~62k in eu-west, avg chunk size 1.2KB, write Q depth 600 -> 446MB queued across proxies. Memory pressure + epoll wake churn could increase p99.

maria: mitigation options: 1) increase proxy keepalive and write buffer sizes (warm config change), 2) recycle a subset of proxy pods to reset stuck epoll contexts, 3) enable per-connection backpressure smoothing in runtime (hot flag), 4) degrade to non-streaming fallback for tiered customers. Thoughts?

jia: ops-runbook-bot, any recommended default from runbook?

ops-runbook-bot: Recommended playbook for streaming-backpressure:
- Immediate: remove 10% of least-loaded proxy pods from rotation and restart.
- Short term: enable write_buffer_smoothing = true for proxy binary (hot reload supported).
- Customer mitigation: move affected customers to batch polling for up to 15 min.
- Monitor: p95/p99, write_queue, tcp_retransmits, epoll_wakeup_rate.

sam: will start recycling proxies in eu-west now. doing a 3-batch staggered restart (10% each).

alex: enabling write_buffer_smoothing flag now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/flags -d '{"write_buffer_smoothing":true}'` (applied to eu-west proxies).

maria: applying kernel net.core.wmem_max bump on one proxy host to test: `sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=262144` then watch.

alex: initial effect: write_queue depth dropped ~35% on restarted pods; p95 improved from 2.6s -> 1.1s within 90s. p99 still elevated at ~6s for some streams.

jia: customer impact update: three enterprise customers reporting intermittent stalls; support has notified them we're mitigating and will follow up. Estimated impacted sessions ~8-12% of eu-west streaming sessions.

sam: rolling restarts round 2 now. also draining connections gracefully to avoid reconnect storm. Using `drain --grace 60s`.

maria: good. track reconnect rate. if reconnect spike > 15% we may need to pause restarts.

alex: watch: reconnects peaked at 9% during batch, now settling to 3%. Good. p99 down to 3.8s overall, some high-tail cases remain on few origin nodes.

jia: traced one client with repeated slow acks; looks like mobile carrier path causing pacing. Could be amplifying the proxy queue oscillation.

maria: next mitigation: enable temporary per-connection max-queued-bytes cap of 256KB to prevent single slow client from starving others. Can we push as hot config?

sam: yes, hot flag available: `max_queued_bytes=262144` applied to edge proxies. pushing to 25% of pool as canary.

alex: applied to canary group. early signals: write_queue variance reduced and p95 stable ~0.9s, p99 ~2.2s for canary nodes.

incident-bot: NOTE: sla-checker flagged potential SLO breach window 03:04-03:18 UTC. Estimated user-facing errors increased by 0.4% during window.

maria: summary for next shift / exec: cause is compounded slow-consumer client patterns + proxy write-buffer oscillation under high concurrency causing tail amplification. Immediate mitigations: staggered proxy restarts, write_buffer_smoothing flag, per-connection queued-byte cap. Outcome: p95 returned near normal, p99 reduced by ~60% but not fully resolved for all origin nodes. Customer impact: 8-12% sessions affected; 3 enterprise customers reported.

jia: notes for follow-up: 1) investigate kernel/epoll churn on origin nodes, 2) evaluate dynamic per-connection pacing in runtime, 3) consider autoscaling policy tweak to prioritize write-buffer headroom during EU morning spikes, 4) add more granular alerting for write_queue variance and epoll wake rate.

sam: logging handoff: I'm going offline in 45m. leaving canary watch up, health checks stable.

maria: thanks. i'm taking post-mitigation lead. will keep watch for 60m, then handoff to night oncall with summary.

alex: adding a quick troubleshooting snippet to thread for ops notes:
```bash
# view worst proxies by queued bytes
kubectl -n infra exec -it proxy-metrics-pod -- /bin/sh -c \"curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep write_queue | sort -n -k2 | tail -n 20\"
# restart batch example
for pod in $(kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=proxy -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | cut -d\" \" -f1 | tail -n +1 | head -n 6); do kubectl -n infra drain $pod --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 && kubectl -n infra delete pod $pod; sleep 30; done
```

maria: final note for handoff: ticket created INC-2026, link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026. Please include p99 charts, affected customers list, and timeline. Handing over to night oncall @alejandra at 04:15 UTC.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded. Next-oncall: alejandra. Severity downgraded to sev4 at 03:45 UTC after steady p99 decline.

maria: (reacted :thumbsup:) will attach logs and the short-term config diffs to the ticket.

alex: (reacted :eyes:) good job everyone.

sam: leaving postmortem notes in INC-2026.

jia: closing customer comms loop, support sent follow-up and offered extended support credits.

maria: thread end — monitoring continues, but no active mitigation steps pending.
